text:
anya: Uploading nsys trace from last night's repro — seeing a tail reg on small-batch workloads. Timeline shows repeated host->device memcpy bursts interleaving with tiny kernels and ~5-10ms CPU gaps where the enqueue thread is idle. https://redwood-traces.internal/2155/run1.qdrep :thinking_face:

matt: Saw the trace. Looks like H2D copies end up on stream 2 but kernels on stream 0 are waiting — even though the code uses async copies. Could be unpinned memory or accidental sync in prefetch path. :mag:

sasha: Quick screenshot: kernel launches are clustered, then memcpy islands, then a host sleep (sched gap). That host sleep aligns with the prefetch completion callback. Might be the fallback path doing a synchronous cudaMemcpy.

anya: Collected with nsys using the same command as the repro run:```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o ~/traces/2155_run1.qdrep --sample=none 
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi 
  --capture-range-end=stop python -m infra.infer_repro --cfg tests/mini_batch.yaml
```

zach: Confirming: our kvcache prefetch has a fallback path that does plain cudaMemcpy (not async) when pinned allocation fails. If pinned allocation is rare on host in that env, we'd see exactly this behavior.

perf-bot: perf-alert: model/opt-quant rollout shows +12% p95 latency on chat-small-batch (week over week). See PERF-DASH-999.

matt: Hypothesis: batching heuristic produces many microbatches (1-2 reqs) leading selector to pick a smaller GEMM kernel with higher launch overhead. Combined with synchronous prefetch copies, this explodes tail latency. cc @sasha

sasha: Two quick experiments to run: 1) force pinned allocations + cudaMemcpyAsync on prefetch stream; 2) increase batching window from 1ms->4ms to let coalescing happen. I'll queue both traces.

anya: I ran pinned+async locally and saw host-side stalls drop ~30% and p95 improved noticeably. Attached diff of nsys timelines: H2D no longer blocks main enqueue thread.

zach: If we make prefetch async we must ensure eviction path doesn't call cudaDeviceSynchronize on eviction completion — that would reintroduce sync. Audit that path.

matt: Also, kernel selector log shows fallback to small_gemm_v2 for M<=64 and seq_len=1. v2 has better peak throughput for tiny matrices but worse launch overhead. Can we prefer small_gemm_v1 for microbatch-heavy scenarios?

sasha: There's a simple rule in heuristics/kernel_selector.cpp around line 120. Proposed quick patch: if (batch_len < 8 && requests_in_window > 2) prefer v1. I'll open a draft PR and run perf.

anya: Repro steps I used (short):
  1) start infra mock with 8 workers and kvcache prefetch on
  2) run: python -m infra.infer_repro --model opt-quant --batch_window_ms 1 --trace-output traces/2155
  3) collect: nsys profile ... (see above)

matt: Note: when changing selector we need perf runs on dedicated infra (multi-tenant noise different). I'll schedule baseline + pinned+async + selector-change on perf infra.

sasha: Plan: run three experiments (baseline, pinned+async prefetch, selector rule). I'll attach traces and a short analysis for each. ETA ~48h.

anya: One small telemetry ask: add a traceview tag to the batcher enqueues that emits request ids so we can correlate prefetch memcpy islands with originating requests in the timeline. Makes debugging these interleaving cases much easier.

perf-bot: noted. Ticket created: PERF-4123 (add trace tags to batcher + audit kvcache memcpy path).

matt: Thanks all. If anyone running the repro sees pinned alloc failures in logs (alloc_pinned: fallback true) ping this thread. We'll prioritize fixes that remove syncs on the hot path. :thumbsup:
